summary: The German Value Investor's "Lululemon Stock: A Once-in-a-Decade Opportunity?" (published 2026-09-30, ~15:59 BST) keeps a HOLD on Lululemon (LULU, ~$100 context price) — fairly valued, not cheap enough to buy. His buy limit would be ~$74. Beyond the call: the setup is a fallen angel — down 80% from ATH to ~$100 (back to April 2018 levels), headline P/E of 8.5 on trailing $12+ EPS, but guidance has been cut three times this year ($13.26 in 2025, then $12.20, $11.05, now $8.75 — a ~30% profit slump) so the forward P/E is really ~12; still cheap versus a 2016–2025 average P/E of 35. Balance sheet is the bull case: zero financial debt, $1.4B net cash (~$12.50/share, 12% of market cap; adjusted P/E just 7.3). The bear evidence: aggressive buybacks at top prices ($318 avg in 2024, $237 in 2025, $141 in H1 2026) destroyed value — a "cry for help" signal on management quality; net income fell 376M to 278M in the quarter while EPS fell less ($3.10 to $2.92) only thanks to buybacks; cash is being burned faster than FCF (H1: $260M FCF vs $700M buybacks); North America revenue fell 12% in Q2 2026 on fewer visitors, lower conversion and smaller baskets; margins under pressure. Scenarios: bull ~$200 fair (~$150 with margin of safety, ~50% upside) on sustained 9%/8% EPS growth; bear ~$36 (-65%) if EPS falls 10%/year for 5 years; weighted expected return ~7% — market-like. Competitors Nike, Adidas mentioned; NN Group video teased as outro. Auto-captions are machine-translated (the creator narrates in English but the caption file contains translation artifacts, e.g., "2023" figures with cut-off averages and "LVMH's balance sheet" for Lululemon's).
